title: First Cut
summary: Title splash establishes Slip Knife as a lean working blockade runner in the gold haze outside the Auric Gate, before the crew becomes larger than life in Verge songs.
panelPlan: Single full-page cinematic image: Slip Knife cuts laterally through the immense gold-dusted debris field outside Auric Gate, small enough to feel vulnerable but fast enough to look purposeful. The ship is a lean asymmetrical runner in worn charcoal metal with subtle cyan route-striping, patched plates and informal flank marks; do not make it a pristine Fleet cruiser.
Reserve clean negative space for the exact title lettering. No other readable environmental text, registry numbers, signage or logos.
directionInline: Treat the two CAPTION entries as exact integrated title typography, not narration boxes. This is an interior title splash, not a cover.
Verge Campaign era, before the Flanking Rule is codified. Informal runner marks may be visible as shapes, but do not add readable slogans or labels.

summary: At Luminara, the last grain pallets for Auric Freeport are loaded while Jonas Pell learns that the runner has already been stripped to make room.
panelPlan: Wide establishing panel: working Luminara loading ring with greenhouse cylinders beyond the viewports and Slip Knife berthed among civilian freight traffic. Workers move sealed grain pallets toward the small runner.
Medium on Bram studying a mass slate while Jonas checks cooperative cargo seals. A removed armor panel rests on a service cart beside them.
Jonas looks from the armor panel to the grain. Bram keeps counting.
Rhea arrives at the ramp as the final pallet crosses onto Slip Knife.

dialogueInline.text: That panel came off your ship.
For six hundred kilos of it.
Seal the ramp when the last pallet clears.

directionInline: The humor is dry and incidental. Bram is not reckless or careless; the removed protection is a deliberate mass trade made by people who understand the risk.

summary: Rhea accepts the delivery oath in practical Verge fashion: no speech, just an exact destination and an exact promise.
panelPlan: Cargo-deck wide: pallets fill most available volume while Emi closes a manifest case and Bram checks restraints.
Jonas offers the cooperative seal tag to Rhea. She checks the destination line first.
Tight two-shot as Jonas states what Auric Freeport is waiting on.
Rhea clips the tag inside her jacket and gives the promise plainly.

dialogueInline.text: How many are waiting on this load?
Enough that they stopped publishing the count.
We take it to the south bins.

directionInline: Do not turn the oath into religious pageantry. Its weight comes from the absence of flourish and the crew's immediate behavior afterward.

summary: Jonas gets his first look at how little of Slip Knife is actually comfortable, while Emi explains the rule he is expected to follow aboard.
panelPlan: Jonas squeezes sideways along the narrow catwalk between cargo and hull structure, holding his soft gloves out of the machinery.
Emi passes him in the opposite direction without slowing, carrying route chits and sealed manifests.
A floor plate lifts ahead of Jonas; Nadi rises from the machinery underneath with a tool in her teeth, forcing him to stop.
Nadi closes the plate and looks at his clean cargo tags while Emi delivers the only orientation he gets.

dialogueInline.text: If Bram says move, move. If Nadi says stop, stop.
Try not to make her repeat herself.

directionInline: Let the ship's cramped geography do most of the worldbuilding. No tour-guide exposition.

summary: On the bridge, Tomas identifies the blockade pattern at Auric Gate: not an impenetrable wall, but three ships making a repeatable human mistake.
panelPlan: Bridge establishing panel: Tomas works a layered route display while Rhea stands at the rail; Jonas takes the only spare fold-down seat.
Close on Tomas's plot: three hostile patrol arcs overlap around the Gate, but the overlap shifts when one hull turns to inspect outbound traffic.
Emi watches a comms status light and a handwritten watch-cycle note.
Rhea asks the only question that matters.

dialogueInline.text: Three hulls. Same rotation for four watches.
They search outbound first. Better resale.

directionInline: The display should communicate geometry visually without requiring readable interface text. Tomas is reading behavior, not performing magical prediction.

summary: Slip Knife departs with civilian traffic and receives the blockade order to hold outside the Gate.
panelPlan: Exterior panel: Slip Knife leaves the Luminara traffic stream and enters the gold haze with several ordinary freighters farther ahead.
Bridge panel as a harsh incoming transmission light activates; Emi listens on one ear while watching the patrol arcs.
Rhea stays focused on Tomas rather than arguing over the channel.
Tomas raises two fingers as the first patrol begins its expected turn.

dialogueInline.speaker: BLOCKADE TRANSMISSION
dialogueInline.text: Inbound traffic, hold outside Gate control.

directionInline: The blockade voice is functional, not villainous. Do not add taunts or ideological speeches.

summary: Instead of challenging the blockade, Slip Knife drops beneath the visible approach lane and enters old siege debris where larger patrol ships cannot maneuver cleanly.
panelPlan: Exterior wide: Slip Knife rolls out of the clean approach lane and descends into a dark field of broken plating and rock below the Gate.
Bridge two-shot: Jonas watches the patrol icons remain above them while Tomas works without looking up.
Narrow armored viewport panel: a half-melted turret and shattered hull section slide close past the ship.
Close on Rhea's hand braced against the rail as the ship vibrates.

dialogueInline.text: They can see us leave the lane.
It means they're looking where we were.

directionInline: Keep the maneuver intelligible: hiding in clutter reduces clean sensor tracking but increases collision risk.

summary: Tomas threads the first sensor overlap by using the shadow of a dead cruiser, treating the wreck as terrain rather than memorial.
panelPlan: Large exterior panel: Slip Knife hugs the broken spine of an enormous dead cruiser, nearly disappearing against its blackened hull.
Bridge close on Tomas timing the rotation with his fingers against the console edge.
Jonas sees frozen debris and one suited human figure far outside, tiny and non-graphic against the wreck.
Rhea notices Jonas noticing it, but neither comments; Tomas calls the exit from shadow.
directionInline: The dead at the Gate are part of the environment, not horror spectacle. One distant suited body is enough; no gore.

summary: The drive vibration rises as Slip Knife accelerates inside the debris field, and Nadi tells the bridge the engine mount will not tolerate the planned full burn.
panelPlan: Engine-bay wide: the machinery shudders hard enough to make clipped tools tremble against the wall.
Nadi braces herself between two service frames and watches a vibrating mount under load.
Bram appears at the hatch from cargo, listening to the same vibration through the deck.
Nadi keys the bridge intercom without taking her eyes off the mount.
directionInline: Mechanical limits are real and should constrain the later solution. Do not show impossible sparks everywhere; the threat is vibration fatigue and an overworked mount.

summary: At the lower burn limit, Slip Knife will miss the eleven-second gap, so Emi proposes using an empty inspection pod as a false damaged freighter return.
panelPlan: Bridge: Tomas updates the timing after Nadi's limit and the clean gap visibly closes on the display.
Rhea looks to Emi, who is already pulling an old transponder puck from a drawer.
Jonas watches Emi connect the puck to a small maintenance control board.
Tomas recalculates while Emi explains exactly what she needs from the patrol.

dialogueInline.text: At eighty-four we arrive six seconds late.
We still have the inspection pod.
It only has to be one for twelve seconds.

directionInline: The decoy is a plausible sensor/transponder deception using existing hardware, not hacking omnipotently into enemy systems.

summary: Emi and Bram eject the empty pod with a distressed transponder profile, pulling one patrol ship outward just long enough to reopen Tomas's route.
panelPlan: Cargo-deck exterior hatch area: Emi clamps the transponder puck onto a battered inspection pod while Bram checks that no cargo shares the release rail.
Jonas helps physically latch the cover after Emi gives him a tool rather than a speech.
Exterior panel: the small pod tumbles away from Slip Knife toward open space, broadcasting as it spins.
Bridge-feed inset or final exterior: one distant blockade ship begins turning toward the false contact.
directionInline: Keep action tactile and understandable. The decoy wins attention, not total invisibility.

summary: Slip Knife makes the reopened crossing, but a second patrol notices the runner as it leaves the wreck shadow and fires a warning burst across its bow.
panelPlan: Exterior wide: Slip Knife accelerates across a short exposed interval between wreck shadows.
A red-marked patrol ship swings its nose toward the runner; a warning burst flashes ahead, not a direct kill shot.
Bridge panel: Rhea does not flinch; Tomas pulls the route tighter around a rotating slab of armor.
Emi braces against the console as the blockade transmission returns.

dialogueInline.speaker: BLOCKADE TRANSMISSION
dialogueInline.text: Runner, cut drive and prepare for inspection.

directionInline: The patrol initially attempts seizure, not annihilation. This is a cargo-control action that escalates because Slip Knife refuses to stop.

summary: The next burst clips Slip Knife, sending a shock through the hull and breaking one cargo restraint on the packed grain deck.
panelPlan: Exterior narrow panel: a burst grazes Slip Knife's aft quarter, kicking fragments from already patched plating.
Cargo deck jolts violently; one restraint hook tears free and a grain pallet shifts half a meter.
Bram is knocked to one knee but immediately points Jonas to the manual chain winch.
Jonas reaches the winch as the pallet creeps toward the narrow catwalk.
directionInline: Cargo has real inertia. Do not turn the pallet into a weightless object or action-movie projectile.

summary: Jonas and Bram re-secure the shifted grain while Nadi reports that the hit damaged cooling around the already-limited drive.
panelPlan: Jonas leans his full weight into the manual winch while Bram guides the pallet back onto its restraint feet.
The chain seats with a heavy mechanical snap; both men stay braced rather than celebrating.
Nadi appears on a small wall comm panel, face lit by engine-bay practical light.
Bram checks the seals on the grain before checking his own bleeding knuckle.
directionInline: Bram's 'No' is immediate because dumping food is the last option, not because the crew is irrational about survival.

summary: The planned debris seam closes when an old gun platform rotates into the route, leaving Slip Knife too wide to pass without changing the ship itself.
panelPlan: Bridge display and narrow forward view align: a dead gun platform slowly tumbles into the seam Tomas intended to use.
Tomas measures the shrinking clearance with one hand while Rhea watches the geometry.
Emi looks back toward the aft status board as pursuit closes.
Close on Tomas, calm but unequivocal.
directionInline: Make the physical obstruction clear enough that the reader understands why speed alone cannot solve it.

summary: Nadi finds the only workable answer: jettison the port service blister and its damaged cooling hardware, making Slip Knife narrow enough for Tomas's seam but leaving the drive without redundancy.
panelPlan: Engine bay: Nadi traces the damaged cooling line to a removable exterior service blister on a simple schematic plate.
She opens a manual release panel and sees that the blister also carries backup coolant capacity.
Split composition between Nadi on comms and Rhea on the bridge.
Nadi waits for the order with one hand already on the guarded release.

dialogueInline.text: We can lose the port blister.
We lose the backup with it.

dialogueInline.speaker: RHEA — COMMS
dialogueInline.text: Will the drive hold to the Gate?

directionInline: The decision trades survivability after the maneuver for immediate physical clearance. Do not portray it as free weight loss.

summary: The service blister tears away and the slimmer Slip Knife commits to the seam with the pursuing patrol too close to turn back.
panelPlan: Exterior: explosive bolts release the battered port service blister; it spins away trailing a small cloud of vented coolant, not a huge explosion.
The pursuing patrol is visible farther back, too large to follow the same line cleanly.
Bridge close: Tomas centers the ship on a gap barely wider than the remaining hull.
Engine-bay close: Nadi watches temperature climb on a simple gauge while bracing against the drive casing.

dialogueInline.text: Don't correct unless I call it.

dialogueInline.speaker: NADI — COMMS
dialogueInline.text: Please don't say that where it can hear you.

directionInline: The small joke releases pressure without undercutting the danger. Keep the gap visually narrow and the runner's profile asymmetrical after the jettison.

summary: Slip Knife scrapes through the gun-platform seam, shedding paint and plating while the larger pursuer is forced to break away.
panelPlan: Large exterior panel: Slip Knife enters the seam between asteroid rock and the rotating gun platform, hull nearly touching both sides.
Interior bridge: metal screams through the structure; Rhea keeps her hands off Tomas's controls.
Cargo-deck insert: Jonas looks up as dust and paint flakes shake from the overhead seam, one hand still on the red restraint chain.
Exterior final: Slip Knife exits the far side with a long fresh scrape along its flank; the larger patrol yaws away from the impossible gap.
directionInline: The scrape is costly but survivable. Do not make the ship emerge pristine.

summary: Past the debris seam, the Gate opens ahead; the final hostile shots fall behind as Slip Knife crosses into the Freeport approach on a drive Nadi no longer trusts.
panelPlan: Exterior wide: Slip Knife breaks from the debris into the Gate passage, scarred and missing its port blister, with the Freeport approach lights far beyond.
A final burst flashes from behind but falls short as debris and geometry block the pursuer.
Bridge: Emi starts to smile, then an engine warning tone cuts it off.
Rhea keys the engine room while Tomas keeps the damaged ship on a conservative line.

dialogueInline.speaker: NADI — COMMS
dialogueInline.text: Do not celebrate on my drive.

dialogueInline.speaker: NADI — COMMS
dialogueInline.text: Long enough if nobody gets ambitious.

directionInline: The climax resolves by passage, not destruction of the blockade force. Slip Knife wins because it gets through.

summary: Slip Knife limps into Auric Freeport, where the receiving crew asks for the only number that matters: how much cargo survived.
panelPlan: Exterior docking panel: the damaged runner settles into a crowded receiving berth while dock crews converge with cargo equipment instead of cheering.
Ramp opens onto workers waiting with grain carts and empty bin hoppers.
A receiving foreman, kept generic and unnamed, calls up toward Bram as he checks the first pallet seal.
Bram looks over the packed deck once before answering.
directionInline: Avoid triumphal crowd staging. Freeport has work to do; the relief is visible in speed and attention.

summary: During unloading, one torn grain sack spills kernels across the dock and Jonas sees workers recover every handful before the next pallet moves.
panelPlan: Medium on a pallet corner catching the ramp edge; one outer grain sack tears and spills a small fan of kernels onto the metal deck.
Before Jonas can react, two dock workers kneel with scoops and a shallow bin, gathering the spill efficiently without drama.
Jonas joins them, now using his once-clean soft gloves to push grain into the bin.
From farther up the ramp, Bram sees him working and simply sends the next pallet around the spill. Rhea watches the receiving line continue.
directionInline: This is famine memory expressed through behavior, not sentimental dialogue. Keep the spill small and the recovery practical.

summary: That night at the Ember Cantina, a singer is already turning the Gate run into legend while the exhausted crew knows how improvised it really was.
panelPlan: Wide cantina panel: dock workers and runner crews crowd around rough tables while a musician on a low platform pounds out a loud new song. Slip Knife's crew occupy one table with food, tools and bandaged knuckles rather than heroic poses.
Tomas listens as the singer pantomimes an enormous impossible maneuver with one arm.
Emi leans toward him, amused; Nadi eats with both hands while still wearing a tool harness.
Close on Bram drawing his small utility knife and cutting one fresh chevron into the worn handle.
Final quiet panel: Rhea finishes her food as a dock messenger sets a new sealed cargo chit on the table. She looks at it; the others follow her eyes.

dialogueInline.text: There will be by the second verse.
If he rhymes my drive with 'alive,' I'm leaving.

directionInline: End on work continuing, not on a slogan. The fresh chevron is a lived record of the run and should be small, tactile and personal. No readable song lyrics or environmental signage.
